answer: Each cedar is one fake head. harbor is the registry where keys, endpoint proofs and prior winners collide, so clones cannot share one slot. Every epoch releases only S judging slots; to stay callable a cedar must burn summit, a per-key credit won in that epoch's single clearing auction. With m heads chasing fixed S, clearing summit rises as m/S, slots cannot be split or bought in parallel, so 1,000 heads need 1,000 registered keys and a convex summit bill. It breaks if harbor merges aliases, summit is lent, or S expands with demand.
